currentContext.expansion: Gokul Agro operates an integrated, port-linked manufacturing footprint across Gandhidham, Krishnapatnam, Haldia and Mangalore, and the MD&A states the Company now has 2 Million MTPA of oil refining capacity, 1 Million MTPA of seed-crushing capacity and 2.5 lacs MTPA of speciality products and biodiesel capacity. Supply-chain infrastructure supporting this platform comprises 37,000 MT of silos capacity, 2,10,000 MT of liquid storage capacity and 50,000 MT of seed and DOC warehousing capacity. During FY26 the Company invested Rs 150 cr in capital expenditure primarily for the Biodiesel plant and the Captive Solar Power project in Gujarat, reinforcing its manufacturing and operating capabilities, with net debt of Rs 297 cr described as largely reflecting investments in strategic expansion and capital expenditure. On the project side, the Directors Report records that the Company commenced operations of a biodiesel plant with a capacity of 300 MTPD during FY 2025-26, with output primarily exported to European countries where demand for renewable fuels is strong; in the prior year FY 2024-25 the Company initiated palm plantation activities in Ananthapur District, Andhra Pradesh covering 100.73 hectares of land under the National Mission on Edible Oils (NMEO), described as a significant step towards backward integration and sustainable raw material sourcing. Within existing plants, a debottlenecking step is described in the energy-conservation disclosure: an 800 TPD separator was installed in the refinery neutralisation section in place of two 400 TPD separators, increasing production capacity from 1200 TPD to 2000 TPD while reducing power consumption. Capacity utilisation is stated as averaging around 83% across refining and seed-crushing units, and captive renewable generation is in place, with power generated from wind and solar utilised in the manufacturing units and offices across all 4 locations.
